full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 24-2-2011 and 2-3-2011 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Nilphamari in Title Appeal No. 79 of 2001 disallowing the appeal, affirming the judgment and decree dated 23-7-2001 (decree signed on 29-7-2001) passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Domar, Nilphamari in Civil Suit No.1 of 1984 should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts giving rise to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus: The opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted the original Other Class Suit No.1 of 1984 in the court of the learned Assistant Judge, Domar, Nilphamari for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession contending inter alia that the suit property originally belong to the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendants Nos. 13-21, Monir Uddin Chowdhury. At the demise of Monir Uddin Chowdhury there was an amicable partition among the heirs of Monir Uddin Chowdhury and by virtue of that amicable partition the plaintiff obtained the 'ka' schedule land. The further case of the plaintiff is such that the predecessor of other defendants, namely Siddique Hossen obtained lease from the father of the plaintiff during his life time and while Siddique Hossen stopped in paying the rent, the father of the plaintiff after filing a suit obtained a decree, against which Siddique Hossen ran up to the Honourable Supreme Court of Bangladesh but being failed purchased the land described in schedule 'Ga' of the plaint from other co-sharers. Monir Uddin Chowdhury and one Azizar Rahman subsequently amicably possessed their shares and by way of compromise the plaintiff, exclusively possessed the suit land and in the month of August, 1971 the predecessor of the defendants Siddique Hossen forcibly entered into the 'Ka' schedule land and creating a boundary erected homestead with the help of the then Pakistan Army who had a camp at Chilahati and Siddique Hossen was a member of the then peace committee which was formed by the occupation force Pakistan Army and out of fear at that time, the plaintiff could not give any resistance to Siddique Hossen, the predecessor of the defendants. Subsequently, after the independence of Bangladesh the plaintiff repeatedly requested the defendants to hand over vacant possession of the suit land but the defendants denied. Finding no other alternative, the plaintiff instituted the original suit for confirmation of title and eviction of the defendants from the suit property. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendants in short is thus, that the predecessor of the defendants never forcibly entered into the suit property and erected homestead therein and the plaintiff out of ill motive to grab the suit property on false allegation filed the original suit. 

 4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after framing six different issues decided all the issues in favour of the plaintiff and decreed the suit on contest by its judgment and decree dated 23-6-1987. 

 5. Being aggrieved the defendants preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 79 of 2001 in the court of the learned District Judge, Nilphamari, which was transmitted to the court of the learned Joint District Judge, Nilphamari for hearing and disposal and the learned appellate court on hearing the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree dated 24-2-2011 disallowed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 8. Mr Ranjan Chakravorty, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that, admittedly the suit property originally belonged to Monir Uddin Chowdhury the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal failed to appreciate that the 'ka' schedule property which consists of 05 decimals of land, was ascertained by a civil court commissioner and that land is under the exclusive possession of the defendants and prior to them, their predecessor Siddique Hossen. The learned Advocate also submits that it is the positive case of the defendants that initially Siddique Hossen was a permissive possessor under the plaintiff's predecessor, Moinuddin Ahmed and since that permissive possession the defendants are possessing the suit property. Subsequently, by two registered sub-kabala deed dated 21-12-1967 and 18-4-1968 the predecessor of the defendant-petitioners Siddique Hossen purchased the 'Ga' schedule property and that the petitioner's predecessor Siddique Hossen and after his death the present petitioners are not the trespassers to the suit land, and Siddique Hossen was not a member of peace committee in the year 1971 and not dispossessed the plaintiff or his predecessor with the help of Pakistan Army and the plaintiff to the suit Motlob Hossen Chowdhury inasmuch as not corroborated his plaint case, the case of the plaintiff is not proved but the learned trial court as well as the appellate court being guided by surmise and conjecture decided the merit of the suit and the subsequent appeal infavour of the plaintiff and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree deserve interference of this court. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Counsel for the petitioners, the learned Counsel .appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party controverting the argument advanced from the side of the learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that, the trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that, admittedly the suit property belonged to the predecessor of the plaintiff, Monir Uddin Chowdhury and in support of the plaintiff's case he has filed the 'bontonnama' by virtue of which the suit property was devolved upon the exclusive possession and title of Monir Uddin Chowdhury. The learned Advocate further submits that the Advocate Commissioner's report which has been marked as Exhibit-'7' has specified the suit property and the concerned CS khatian vide Exhibit-1, it's map vide Exhibit-2, conclusively proved that the contention of the plaintiff is supported by tangible documentary evidence and on the other hand, the defendants by adducing any cogent evidence measurably have failed to prove that their predecessor Siddique Hossen was in possession of the suit property by way of getting permission from the plaintiff's predecessor Monir Uddin Chowdhury. The learned Advocate also submits that the defendants have also failed to produce any paper which can be treated authentic in support of the defendant's case and since the plaintiff to the suit at the relevant time was very much sick and was not able to move his normal pursuit. PW 1 Monjurul Hoque Chowdhury on behalf of the plaintiff, who happens to be a close relative of the plaintiff gave his testimony supporting the pleadings of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate argued that the plaintiff who is the uncle and father-in-law of PW 1 requested him (PW 1) to depose in the court and accordingly, PW 1with the permission of the court made his deposition and he has been thoroughly cross-examined from the side of the defendants and there is no objection at the relevant time from the side of the defendants as to the authority of PW 1, even if; no objection was raised in proving the documents of the plaintiff before the court at the time of trial and in this context the learned counsel referred a decision of our Apex Court reported in 62 DLR (AD) 242 with regard to concurrent observation and findings of the courts below in connection with the right, title, interest, possession and dispossession etc. of the plaintiff to the suit land. The learned Advocate lastly submits that there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice from the side of the learned appellate court by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. 

 10. In order to appreciate the submission advanced from the sides of the learned counsels for the parties, having gone through the pleadings of the parties, the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court in Other Suit No. 01 of 1984, the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court in Title Appeal No. 79 of 2001, the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties and the documents produced with all other connected papers it transpires that it is an admitted position that the suit property appertaining to mouza Veladaburi under Domar Upozilla corresponding to CS Khatian No. 428 and subsequent RS khatian No. 564, Plot No. 8370 consists of 10 decimals of land, out of which 05 decimals of land originally belonged to the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff and the defendants No. 13-21 namely Monir Uddin Chowdhury. It is the specific contention of the plaintiff that after the death of Monir Uddin Chowdhury the legal heirs entered in to an amicable partition and by way of that partition the suit land had been owning and possessing by the plaintiff. It is the pleading's case of the plaintiff that the plaintiff's father Monir Uddin Chowdhury during his life time rented the suit land in favour of the original defendant's predecessor Md Siddique and at the refusal to pay the rent Monir Uddin Chowdhury obtained a decree against the predecessor of the defendants and by way of execution of that decree the predecessor of the plaintiff realized the arear rents from Siddique Hossen. 

 13. Apart from this, PW 1 Monjurul Hoque Chowdhury, who is the son-in-law of the plaintiff, in his testimony testified that his uncle as well as father-in-law is sick having pain in his waist and that is why he is giving deposition on behalf of his father-in-law. P.W. 1 in his examination-in-chief, specifically corroborated the plaint case and during his cross-examination in a reply to a question from the side of the defendants this witness categorically testified that during the war of liberation in the year 1971 AD the predecessor of the defendants, Siddique Mia dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit property, who was a member of peace committee. PW 2 AKM Zakaira Bosunia in his testimony testified that, he knows the parties and the suit land and the plaintiff has been dispossessed from the suit land by the defendants in the month of August, 1971 and the suit land is 05 decimals, arise out of Plot No. 8370. During cross examination in a reply to a question from the side of the defendants, PW 2 testifies that after 25th March of 1971, he was at Chilahati and the Pakistan Army had a camp there. In another stage of cross-examination, PW 2 categorically testifies that Siddique Miah with the help of other non-bengali including one Lutfor dispossessed the plaintiff 'and after dispossession the suit land has been 'gheraoed' by "chagar". The Civil Court Commissioner Md Asaduzzaman Miah has been deposed as court witness and this witness in his disposition testifies that due to missing of the original copy, he has produced the photocopy of the report. This witness has identified the photocopy which has been marked as Exhibit -7 (ka) as secondary evidence by the learned trial court. 

 20. In the result; the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 24-2-2011 and 2-3-2011 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Nilphamari in Title Appeal No. 79 of 2001 disallowing the appeal affirming the judgment and decree dated 23-7-2001 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Domar, Nilphamari in Title Suit No.1 of 1984 is hereby affirmed.

parties:
Abu Taher and others……….Appellants
Vs.
Rustom Ali being dead his heirs: Noor Miah, Aslam Miah being dead his heirs and Yunus Miah being dead his heirs: Abdul Mannan and others……….Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. This appeal by leave obtained by the plaintiff -appellant has been preferred against the judgment and order dated 30.05.2011 passed by a single bench of the High Court Division in civil Revision No. 4847 of 2004 affirming the judgment and decree dated 4.9.2004 passed by the Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 75 of 1985 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 2.5.1985 passed by the then Munsif Upazila Court, Laksham, now Assistant Judge, Laksham, Comilla, in Title Suit No. 479 of 1983. 

 2. Short facts necessary for the disposal of this appeal are that the appellants as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 479 of 1983 in the Court of the then Munsif, Upazila court, Laksham, now Assistant Judge, Laksham, Comilla for declaration of Title in the suit land contending inter alia that the suit land originally belonged to Fateh Ali, Mokaram Ali, Hasan Ali and Safar Ali in equal share which was recorded as such in the C.S. record. Mokaram Ali died leaving behind the other quo-sharers as heirs who had been using the same as their homestead. There being shortage of space Fateh Ali and Safar Ali moved elsewhere constructing new homestead in ejmali leaving Hasan Ali as the only owner in possession in the said homestead. Hasan Ali died leaving behind 2 sons Gafur Ali and Kalu Miah but in the S.A. Khatian No. 563 the name of Gafur Ali and Kalu Miah were recorded along with the names of defendants No. 1-3 and 11, (Sekander Ali predecessor of defendant No. 6, Safor Ali, predecessor of defendant No.7 and Nuruzzaman, predecessor of defendant No. 8-10). This wrong recording in the S.A. Khatian transpired recently on the basis of which the defendants denied the title of the plaintiffs who are in of the suit land for more than 12 years. The defendants have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. Hence the suit 

 3. The defendants No. 1, 2(Ka) and 3 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all material statements made in the plaint, contending inter alia that the suit land originally belonged to C.S recorded owners Fateh Ali, Hasan Ali, Makaram Ali and Safar Ali; that for arrears of rent the suit land was put into auction and the landlord purchased the same upon evicting the tenants. Thereafter Alimuddin and his son Sekander Ali executed a Kabuliyat in favour of the landlord and took settlement of the suit land from the Zaminder and had been paying rents regularly. Hasan Ali being a relative of Alimuddin and Sekander Ali were allowed to leave in 6 decimals of land on compassionate ground and as such he was a mere licensee having no right, and interest in the suit land; that the plaintiffs being heirs of Hasan Ali has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. The S.A. and R.S. records were correctly prepared on the basis of right, title, interest and possession of the suit land. The defendants donated some Land to the local mosque by a deed of waqf and constructed the mosque in front of their homestead. The plaintiffs had no right, title, interest and possession as such the prayer of the plaintiffs should be dismissed. 

 4. The trial court upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 2.5.1985. Against the same the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 75 of 1985 before the learned District Judge, Comilla. The appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Comilla who by his judgment and decree dated 4.9.2004 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree o the trial court. The plaintiffs thus move( the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4847 of 2004 and obtained Rule which has been ultimately discharged by judgment and order dated 30.5.2011 by a single Bench of the High Court Division affirming the judgment and decree of till lower appellate court. 

 7. Per contra Mr. Farid Ahmed the learned advocate appearing on behalf of defendant-respondents submits that there is no illegality in allowing the appeal by lower appellate court and affirming the same by the High Court Division as the plaintiffs hopelessly failed to prove their title as well as possession in the suit land. He submits that the suit property was sold in auction pursuant to order dated 15.5.1939 in certificate case No. 2 of 1938-1939 and pursuant to the said order the purchaser took possession of the suit land on 15.5.1941 and thereby the title and possession of the original tenants has been extinguished. He also submits that PW 1 himself in his cross examination admitted that his grandfather and others were evicted from the suit and thereafter the same was leased out to Alimuddin and Sekander; that the S.A. and R.S. records were correctly prepared and the defendants having title and possession in the suit land had been paying rents to the Jamimders as well as to the Government vide exhibit B and C series. He also submits that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession in the suit land by producing any scrap of paper as against the sale certificate in pursuant to order dated 15.5.1941. Lastly, Mr. Ahmed submits that the lower appellate court being the last court of fact specifically found title and possession of the defendants in the suit land pursuant to admission of the plaintiffs No. 2 and 3 (PWS) that they as to the title of defendant No. 3 and their purchased 6 decimals of land from defendant No. 3 by kabala dated 27.11.1968 much earlier to institution of the suit in 1983. This admission of purchase is nothing but actually admitting the title of the defendants in the suit land. Thus he submits that the High Court Division rightly affirmed the judgment of the blower appellate court: 

 8. On this back drop we have gone through the materials on record and considered the submissions as noted above. Admittedly it is a suit for declaration simpliciter. So it is the duty of the plaintiffs to prove their title in the suit land. Question of possession though is one of the main factors but that may come in such suit as subsidiary evidence on the principle that possession follows title. On perusal of the judgment of the lower appellate court, which has been affirmed by the High Court Division, it appears that upon analysing the evidence of PWs the last court of fact found that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title in the suit land. PW1 in his evidence said that he could not remember whether they paid any rent to the Bangladesh Government any time before or after the suit has been instituted in 1982. 

 10. Apart from the above upon going through the evidence of DWs it appears that DW 1 in his deposition categorically stated that the plaintiff’s No. 1, 2 and 3 purchased 6 decimals of land from the defendants by Kabola which PW1 denied in his cross examination but plaintiff no. 2 and 3 admitted the same. From the judgment of the trial court it appears that the said court also found that 'the defendants sold 6 decimals of land to the plaintiffs and 24 decimals of land to other persons. On this score on perusal of exhibit-2, a document filed by the plaintiffs, it appears that the denial of PW-1 as to purchase of 6 decimals of land from the defendants does not have any leg to stand. Thus when the plaintiffs purchased the suit property or any portion thereof from the defendants it is clear that unless the title of the defendants is admitted the plaintiffs could not purchase the same. On the face of such admission of defendant's title the decree of the trial court was not proper which the court of appeal below, upon discussing the evidence on record correctly reversed. Thus we cannot but hold that the court of appeal below as well as the High Court Division did not commit any error/illegality in passing the judgment in favour of the defendants and thereby dismissing the suit.

parties:
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works, Bangladesh and others ----- Appellants
VS
Md. Sharif Uddin and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J: This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 8-6-2011 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3070 of 2010 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated 5-4-2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Sixth Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 07 of 2009 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 28-6-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 234 of 2003 dismissing the same. 

 Al-haj Md Serajuddin as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. (number not stated) of 1998 renumbered as Title Suit No. 234 of 2003 in the Additional Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka praying for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession on removing the construction standing on the suit property. His case, in short, is that he purchased the land of 'Ka' schedule to the plaint with two storied building, garage, different plants situated on SA Dag No. 10 of Mouza-Kakrail under previous Lalbagh Police Station now Ramna within Dhaka Collector ate from Syed Farooq Mirja, son of Syed Fakrul Hasan Mirja in 1971. After purchase, the plaintiff got his name mutated and had been paying taxes regularly. While the plaintiff was abroad, the 'Ka' schedule was wrongly declared abandoned property. Having come to know of the aforesaid fact, the plaintiff filed an application to the Government of Bangladesh and the Government having been satisfied released the suit property in favour of the plaintiff and issued memo dated 19-6-1983 from the office of defendant No. 3 but defendant No. 1 did not return the land shown in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint. Consequently, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1988 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Fourth Court, Dhaka, which was decreed on 17-12-1988. After that, the plaintiff requested defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to deliver 'Kha' schedule land to him on a number of dates from 26-3-1989 up to 3-5-1997 and lastly, on 8-7-1997 but defendant No. 1 did not vacate or deliver 'Kha' schedule land to the plaintiff. As such the plaintiff issued legal notice upon defendant No. 1 on 1-9-1997. But defendant No. 1 did not pay any heed to the said request made by the plaintiff and consequently, the suit was filed. Along with plaint, the plaintiff filed sketch map showing position of the garage. During pendency of the suit, the sole-plaintiff died and his heirs were substituted as the plaintiffs. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 3 by filing written statements denying all the material statements made in the plaint. It appears that at first defendant No. 3 filed written statement on 30-3-2000 and subsequently on 2-5-2000. In the first written statement, it has been written by defendant No.3 that the suit land was allotted to defendant No. 1, vide memo No.2FV-123/72/2103 dated 9-12-1974 at a rental of Taka 1,000 per month and later on, vide memo No. Sef-V/1M/D7/ 70 (PT)/402 dated 3-8-1984 to the Ministry of Home Affairs for using the same for the police department. Since then police department had been enjoying the suit schedule-B land. It is further stated that Title Suit No. 53 of 1988 was decreed against defendant No. 3 on contest and ex parte against defendant Nos. 1 and 2. The aforesaid suit was filed by a person who had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. Summons of the aforesaid suit was not served upon defendant Nos. 1 and 2. The garage mentioned in the instant suit is unspecified and, as such, Civil Court Commissioner is required to be appointed to identify the location of the garage. It is further stated that defendant No. 1 has been possessing the property for more than 20 years and, as such, acquired title by adverse possession. In the second written statement, the Government stated that the suit land had been vested in the Government as per provision of PO (President's Order) No. 16 of 1972 as abandoned property by gazette notification No. 9762 (8) at serial No. 10 according to the provision of Ordinance LIV of 1985 on 23-9-1986 and it was allotted to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and they have been possessing the suit schedule-B property. 

 5. Against the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 07 of 2009 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. On transfer, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the then learned Additional District Judge, Sixth Court, Dhaka, who by his judgment and order dated 5-4-2010 allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 8. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the leave appellants, submits that the plaintiffs in the plaint alleged that they had been dispossessed in 1974 and Title Suit No. (number not stated) of 1998 renumbered as Title Suit No. 234 of 2003 having been filed on 19-2-1998 beyond the statutory period of limitation for recovery of possession, the plaintiffs are not entitled to a decree for recovery of possession in the instant suit. He also submits that the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 52 of 1988 for permanent injunction against the appellants and that decree was passed restraining the appellants from changing the nature and character of the suit land and that the plaintiff of that suit had not asserted his possession in the suit land ('Kha' schedule land to the plaint) and, as such, the decree passed in Title Suit No. 52 of 1988 is of no avail to the plaintiffs and even that suit for permanent injunction was also filed beyond the statutory period of limitation of 12 years from his dispossession in 1974. 

 The subject matter of the instant suit being a garage and whether the same is within the purchased land of the plaintiffs or beyond their purchased land being the subject matter of local investigation with reference to their title deeds and in the instant case the plaintiff having not taken any initiative for local investigation, the Court of appeal below illegally decreed the suit and the High Court Division committed error of law in upholding the said decree. 

 The plaintiff alleged that they have been dispossessed in the year 1974 and they having filed an earlier suit being Title Suit No. 52 of 1988 and in the said suit they having not prayed for recovery of possession from the defendant, the plaintiff is not entitled to a decree for recovery of possession in the instant suit in respect of which they have allegedly been dispossessed in the year 1974." 

 12. It transpired from the plaint that the original plaintiff, Al-haj Md Serajuddin purchased the suit land under Holding No.10, New Baily Road in 1971. After the death of the original plaintiff his heirs were substituted in his place as the plaintiffs. They claimed that the suit land is part and parcel of Holding No. 10, New Baily Road and not Holding No. 10/A, New Baily Road. The plaintiffs alleged that the defendants dispossessed them from the suit land treating it as an abandoned property. 

 13. Admittedly, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1988 for permanent injunction against (1). Superintendent of Police, Special Branch, 10/A, New Baily Road, Police Station-Ramna, Dhaka, (2) Deputy Inspector General, Special Branch, 10/A, New Baily Road, Police Station-Ramna, Dhaka and (3). Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works. The plaint of Title Suit No.53 of 1988 was not exhibited. From judgment delivered in Title Suit No.53 of 1988, we find that the learned Assistant Judge, Fourth Court, Dhaka, while describing the case of the plaintiff stated, amongst others, as under: 

 14. From the aforesaid averment of the plaint, it appears that even in 1978 the sole plaintiff Al-haj Serajuddin was out of possession of the suit land prior to filing of Title Suit No. 53 of 1988 for permanent injunction. 

 15. From the judgment of Title Suit No. 53 of 1988, we find that the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works by filing written statement asserted that the disputed 'Kha' schedule land is part and parcel of Holding No. 10/A, of New Baily Road. Defendant No.3 further asserted that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had been in possession of the suit land ('Kha' schedule land). Having gone through the judgment delivered in Title Suit No. 53 of 1988, we find that the learned Assistant Judge, Fourth Court, Dhaka, restrained the defendants of Title Suit No.53 of 1988 from changing the nature and character of 'Kha' schedule land to the plaint by a decree of permanent injunction. From the judgment, it appears that the plaintiff himself admitted that he was out of possession of 'Kha' schedule land when the suit for permanent injunction was filed. 

 16. Subsequently, the plaintiff filed present Title Suit No. 234 of 2003. The High Court Division having considered the documentary evidence came to a finding that the plaintiff acquired title from the original owner of the suit property who was a non-Bengali. The High Court Division also found that the defendants had no title to the suit land and that they were restrained by an order of permanent injunction for making construction or renovation in the suit land. The High Court Division also found that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had been possessing the suit land on the strength of their possession in the garage defying the decree of the Court passed in Title Suit No. 53 of 1988. 

 17. We have already noticed that even in the plaint of Title Suit No. 53 of 1988 for permanent injunction, the plaintiff Al-haj Md Serajuddin, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff-respondents of Title Suit No. 234 of 2003, stated that he was out of possession of the 'Kha' schedule land. Subsequently, the present suit was filed for declaration of title and recovery of possession. 

 19. Having gone through the record, the judgment delivered in Title Suit No. 53 of 1988 and the evidence of PW 1 given in Title Suit No. 234 of 2003, we find that the plaintiff had been out of possession of the suit land ('Kha' schedule land) according to their admission from 1974. The present suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession was filed in 1998. Therefore, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation. The plaintiff was required to file the suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession within 12 years from the alleged date of dispossession but they have been failed to do so and, as such, they are not entitled to get a decree for recovery of possession. 

 21. In the case of Syed Moin Ahmed vs Khondkar Mohiuddin 19 DLR 912, it has been held that under Article 142 of the limitation Act, it is the duty of the plaintiff first to prove to the satisfaction of the Court that he was in possession of the suit premises within 12 years prior to the filing of the suit and if he fails to do so he cannot get decree for declaration of title and recovery of possession. 

 23. On consideration of the cases referred to above, it appears that in a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession, the plaintiffs in addition to proving their title to the suit land must prove that the suit has been filed within 12 years from the alleged date of dispossession. In the case in hand, the plaintiffs miserably failed to prove that the suit has been filed within 12 years from the alleged date of dispossession. 

 24. In the light of the findings, we are of the view that the High Court Division erroneously decreed the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession.

parties:
Ashad Ali and others ------ Defendant-Appellant-Petitioners
Versus
Nurerzaman and others ------ Plaintiff-Respondent-Opposite parties
full_judgment:
Mr. S.M. Emdadul Hoque, J.:- On an application of the petitioner Ashad Ali and others under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos.1 to 14 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 30.08.2001 passed by the Joint District Judge, Court, Lakshmipur in Title Appeal No.42 of 1995 affirming those dated 26.09.1995 passed by the Assistant Judge, Ramgali, Lakshhmipur in Other Class Suit No.250 of 1993 should not be set-aside. 

 2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the present opposite party Nos.1 to 14 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.215 of 1993 before the Joint District Judge, Lakshmipur for a declaration that the ex-parte decree dated 10.04.1984 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Lakshmipur in Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 is void, collusive and illegal and without any summons. The present petitioner as defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint and claimed that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and is barred by principle of waiver, acquiesces and estoppels. 

 6. Against the said judgment and decree of the trial court the defendant-petitioners preferred Title Appeal No.42 of 2005 before the learned District Judge, Lakshmipur. Ultimately the said appeal was heard by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Lakshmipur who after hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court by its judgment and decree dated 30.08.2001. 

 9. Mr. Abul Hossain Azadi, the learned Advocate argued that though the trial court set aside the judgment and decree dated 10.04.1984 in Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 but it is found that no order of restoration of the suit in its original file and number and when an ex-parte decree is set-aside then the original suit must be restored to its original file and number relying upon the decision reported in 43 DLR (HCD)- 48. He further argued that since both the Courts set-aside the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 in such a case his only submission is that the said suit must be restored to its original file and number for disposal of the same afresh. 

 10. Mr. Muhammad Salahuddin, the learned Advocate has also conceded the said argument of the learned Advocate of the petitioner. He argued that as per decision of the case reported in 43 DLR (HCD)-48 the Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 may be restored to its original file and number for disposal of the same afresh but the Rule may be discharged. 

 "In that view of the matter we hold. that the summons were not duly served upon the petitioners in accordance with law and the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law in his decision resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No.61 of 1987 and rejecting the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the above circumstances we feel that ends of justice will he met, if we set aside the ex-parte decree dated 29.10.1987 and restore the original suit to its file and number." 

 12. Considering the aforesaid facts and decision it is my view that since the court set-aside the ex-parte decree of the Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 so consequently the said should be restored. 

 13. On perusal of the record it is found that the ex-parte decree dated 10.04.1984 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Lakshmipur in Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 but it appears that the said judgment and decree was set-aside by the Assistant Judge. In normal course the Assistant Judge has no authority to interfere with the judgment and decree passed by the superior court i.e. the Subordinate Judge. It appears that by Miscellaneous Order No.67 dated 25.11.1993 of the learned District Judge the suit was transferred to the Senior Assistant Judge. It also appears that the opposite parties filed the said suit before the Subordinate Judge and perhaps when the pecuniary jurisdiction has been increased then the said matter may be sent to the Court of Assistant Judge by the learned District Judge. Though it is not the disputed question in the instant case, but since it is found that the Assistant Judge interfere with the judgment of the superior court i.e. the Subordinate Judge, so, it should be considered whether the inferior Court can hear the said matter. It appears that perhaps firstly, may be for increasing the pecuniary jurisdiction the trial court has empowered to hear the aforesaid suit, since it appears that the learned District Judge vide administrative order No.67 dated 25.11.1993 transferred the said suit to the Assistant Judge. Secondly, if any fraud committed in obtaining any decree or order in any case then the Assistant Judge can consider the matter though earlier decree or order passed by the superior Court. 

 14. Mr. Salahuddin, the learned Advocate argued that the fraud vitiates everything and since without any summons the plaintiffs of the earlier suit i.e. the present petitioners obtained ex-parte decree in Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 in such a case the Assistant Judge, can interfere with the said matter. He further argued that the present opposite- parties rightly filed the case before the Subordinate Judge when the said Court had pecuniary jurisdiction but when the pecuniary jurisdiction having been increased, the learned District Judge by its administrative order sent the suit to the Assistant Judge for hearing. It appears that the trial Court found that the said ex-parte decree obtained by committing fraud and without any summons in such a case the Assistant Judge is empowered to set aside the ex-parte decree passed by the superior Court. 

 16. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the discussions made above. The Rule is discharged with modification of the order. The impugned judgment and decree dated 30.08.2001 passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Lakshmipur in Title Appeal No.42 of 2005 affirming those dated 26.09.1995 passed by the Assistant Judge, Ramgati, Lakshmipur in Other Class Suit No.250 of 1993 are hereby upheld subject to restore the Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 to its original file and number. 

 17. Since Title Suit No.1260 of 1981 is a long pending case the trial court is directed to dispose of the suit as early as possible preferably within 6 months from the date of receipt of this judgment in accordance with law.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 422 of 2010
lawyer:
Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner
Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Principal and Secretary, Nawabgonj Government College, Nawabgonj ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Mahabuba Khatun (Dolly) and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana, J. This Civil Petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 21.07.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 358 of 2002 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 05.02.2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Nawabgonj in Other Class Suit No. 57 of 1987 dismissing the suit. The plaintiff-respondent herein filed the above mentioned Other Class Suit No. 57 of 1987 for declaration of title and partition. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that 4.02 acres of land as described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint originally belonged to 3 brothers, namely, Ashutosh Chatyapadhya, Sharat Chandra Chatyapadhya and Monimdra Chatyapadhya in equal share and the C.S. Khatian was accordingly prepared in their names. That after partition of Pakistan and India Sharat Chandra Migrated to India and arranged an exchange of his share i.e. .95 acre out of schedule 'Ka' land with Indian land of one Ishahaque Mia-the father of the plaintiffs. That for effecting the exchange Sharat Chandra executed a power of attorney in favour of one Harun-ar-Rashid. Harun-ar-Rashid having obtained necessary permission from the then District Collector, Rajshahi, executed and registered a deed of exchange dated 13.10.1952 in favour of Ishahaque Mia. Thus Ishahaque Mia having acquired title and possession in the suit land had been in possession and enjoyment of the same for long 20 years within the knowledge of all including the defendants, Nawabgonj Government College and others. That Ishahaque Mia while in possession of the suit land executed a power of attorney in favour of Harun-ar-Rashid who being so empowered executed and registered two hiba-bil-ewaj deeds dated 09.10.1974 transferring the said .94 acre of land of Ishahaque Mia in favour of his daughters, the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 4. Thus the plaintiffs acquired the suit land and since acquisition they have been in possession of the same by paying rent to the government to the knowledge of all including the defendants. That the defendant college subsequently purchased 2/3rd share of 'Ka' schedule land from Ashutosh and Monindra and has been in ejamali possession of that land with Ishahaque Mia and thereafter with the plaintiffs. That the 'Ka' schedule land has never been partitioned by metes and bounds among these co-sharers. That only in the month of October, 1985 when an employee of the plaintiffs went to pay rent in the local Tahsil Office the Tahsildar disclosed that the land was recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 College in R.S. Khatian and was finally published. That this R.S. record of the land in the name of the college in 16 annas share is wrong and collusive. That on the basis of this wrong recording the defendant college claimed title in the entire 'Ka' schedule land and thus the title of the plaintiffs in the suit has been clouded and hence the suit. 

 2. The defendant college and the government contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. These defendants admit the title of 3 C.S. recorded tenants and subsequently also of Ishahaque Mia in the 'Ka' schedule land. But their case is that the defendant college being established in the then newly created Nawabgonj Sub-Division purchased 95 1/2 decimals of land of 'Ka' schedule from Ashutosh Chattapadhya by a registered sale deed dated 23.02.1957 and also purchased the other 95 1/2 decimals of land from Monindra Chatyapadhya Chandra by registered sale deed dated 12.04.1957. That the share of Sharat Chandra was transferred to Ishahaque Mia by way of exchange and the said Ishahaque Mia transferred his 95 1/2 decimals of land to the college by an oral gift in presence of many and the college authority accepted it with gratitude. These defendants stated also that out of 4.02 acres of land described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint 2.86 acres of land only finally stood as rest 1.16 acres fell into road and ditches. That the college authority thus, is in possession of 2.86 acres of land of the 'Ka' schedule to the knowledge of all including the plaintiffs. This land has been duly recorded in the name of the college in R.S. khatian. The college authority has erected wall on the west and northern side of the R.S. plot few years ago. The college authority is in possession of the suit land for more than 12 years and as such they have acquired title by adverse possession also. That the plaintiffs have filed this suit on false claim suppressing the real facts. 

 3. Before the trial court the plaintiffs examined 7 witnesses and the defendant examined 3 witnesses. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by the parties, dismissed the suit holding, inter-alia, that the suit land is admittedly in possession of the college and that there is no allegation of forcible dispossession by the college and that the plaintiffs created the hiba-bil-ewaj and sale deeds from a person having no title to the suit land and that too after the same had been in possession by the college for more than twelve years. 

 4. On appeal the High Court Division set aside the findings and decision of the trial court and decreed the suit making observations and findings to the effect that the plaintiffs being daughters of the admitted co-sharers have succeeded in proving their title to the extent of 1/3rd share in the land described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint and that the defendants could not prove their claim that the father, of the plaintiffs transferred his 1/3rd share in the 'Ka' schedule land in favour of the defendant college by oral gift and that the defendant college could not prove also its claim that the college has acquired title in this land by adverse possession also and that the recording of the 'Ka' schedule land in the name of the defendant college in 16 annas in R.S. Khatian has been wrong. 

 7. We find that the High Court Division, on meticulous examination of the evidence adduced by both the parties, rightly found that the contesting defendants could not prove at all their case that Ishahaque Mia the admitted co-sharer of the 'Ka' schedule land-gifted his 1/3rd share in favour of the defendant college orally. The High Court Division, on consideration of evidence and facts and circumstances and making elaborate discussion found also that the contesting defendants' claim that the defendant college has acquired title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession also-has not been proved at all. 

 8. We have gone through the evidence on record. We find nothing to disagree with the above findings and decision of the High Court Division. It is admitted that Ishahaque Mia became the owner of the 1/3rd share of C.S. recorded tenant Sharat Chandra Chatyapadhya by way of exchange and he was also in possession of these 1/3rd share of the schedule 'Ka' land. The plaintiffs are the four daughters of this Ishahaque Mia. The trial court though made some observations that the plaintiffs could not prove their case that they acquired these 1/3rd share of their father by two registered hiba-bil-ewaj deeds, but the High Court Division found that the plaintiffs have proved their title in these 1/3rd share of Ishahaque Mia. The High Court Division rightly made observations to the effect that the plaintiffs though could not produce the original copy of their title deeds, namely, heba-bilewaj deeds and also the power of attorney executed by their father Ishahaque Mia in favour of Harun-ar-Rashid and gave explanations of failure to file those original deeds, but in consideration of the fact that the plaintiffs, being natural heirs of the vendor Ishahaque Mia, had no reason to create those documents in respect of their heritable property for maintaining a partition suit against co-sharer in joint possession. We find these observations of the High Court Division also reasonable. It is in evidence that Ishahaque Mia had four daughters the plaintiffs only, he had no son. Any other distant relation of Ishahaque Mia is not coming to raise any claim in respect of the property of Ishahaque Mia. These facts and circumstances also supports the genuineness of the plaintiffs' title deeds. 

 9. However, we find that the High Court Division, on careful examination and consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties and on making elaborate discussion rightly arrived at the decision that in this suit the plaintiffs have successfully proved their title and also possession in 1/3rd share of the schedule 'Ka' land and that the defendants could not prove their case that Ishahaque Mia orally gifted his 1/3rd share in schedule 'Ka' land in favour of the defendant college and also their further case that the defendant college has acquired title in the 1/3rd share of Ishahaque Mia by adverse possession. The impugned judgment of the High Court Division is well reasoned and well written one.
case_type_name: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal

parties:
Nargis Aktar ------ Defendant-Respondent-Petitioner
Vs.
Md Jalaluddin and others ------ Defendant-Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as, to why the judgment and decree dated 27-3-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.250 of 2005 allowing the appeal reversing those of dated 19-4-2005 and 26-4-2005 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 352 of 2004 rejecting the plaint under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party No.1 as plaintiff filed the original suit being Title Suit No. 352 of 2004 in the 1 St court of learned Assistant Judge, Dhaka for a declaration that the appointment of the defendant No. 1 as Headmistress of Hazrat Shah Ali High School is illegal contending inter-alia that the son of the plaintiff is a student of the High School and being the guardian and a local elite person the plaintiff is a voter from the guardian category in the school. The defendant No. 1 was an illegally appointed Head-mistress of the School having no required qualification for the post and practicing fraud sup-pressing the defendant No.1 has been appointed as Headmistress of the School and with-drawing the salary of the post. During pendency of the original suit the defendant No.1 filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejecting the plaint and after hearing the learned trial court allowed the application and rejected the plaint of the suit vide order dated 19-4-2005. 

 6. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned court of appeal below during disposal of the appeal committed illegality and that the impugned judgment and decree is not a proper judgment and decree of reversal. The learned Advocate further submits that the appointment of the defendant-petitioner is legal and on compliance of the Rules of Non-Government Institution Instruction Manual issued from the ministry of education the appointment was completed. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiff-opposite party has no locus standi to institute the original suit under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and secondly the plaintiff before institution of the suit without exhausting the proper forum to seek redress of his grievances filed the original suit and as a result of which the learned trial court was quite justified to reject the plaint under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate lastly submits that no fruitful result can be given from a decree by a civil court in the instant nature of suit and the learned appellate court without proper appreciation of law decided the merit of the appeal illegally which deserve interference of this court. 

 7. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule controverted the arguments advanced from the side of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and submits that there is no ingredient for rejection of the plaint under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the learned appellate court below rightly after proper appreciation of law and materials on record reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court rebutting the findings of the trial court adverting the relevant provisions of law in consultation with the pleadings of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff-opposite-party have every locus standi to institute the suit under the purview of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and if the relief is granted by the civil court that would be a fruitful result for the plaintiff-opposite party. The plaintiff after exhausting the legal requirements for filing a civil suit before a competent court of law instituted the suit. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party in this context pointed out the facts of the case and content of the pleading which was brought by the plaintiff. Learned Advocate has drawn the notice of the court in paragraph Nos. 2, 3, 8, 9 and 11 of the plaint which are related with the locus-standi of the plaintiff and the cause of action of the suit. The learned Advocate lastly submits that after serving legal notice upon the defendants while the plaintiff did not obtain any relief he was constrained to file the original suit. The learned trial court misconstrued the actual position of law as well as the content of the pleadings in its true perspective and subsequently the appellate court below rightly appreciated the law and acted under the provisions laid down in Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in compliance of that reversed the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge and there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. 

 8. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the case records, connected papers, impugned judgment and decree along with the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in Title Suit No. 352 of 2004. 

 9. On perusal of the connected papers it transpires that during pendency of the original suit the defendant-petitioner submitted an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint. In the said application the defendant No.1 states that her appointment in the post of Headmistress of the institution is legal and after compliance of all legal formalities and fulfillment of requirements she has been appointed as Headmistress of the school but the plaintiff in collusion with the interested corner instituted the suit on false allegation having no locus-standi to file the suit. The learned trial court being satisfied rejected the plaint vide judgment and order dated 19-4-2005. 

 10. Being aggrieved the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.250 of 2005 and the appellate court below at the time of disposal of the appeal finding the status of the plaintiff and locus standi to prefer civil suit under the purview of section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure in a civil court reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 27-3-2007. 

 Under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 any person entitled to any legal character, or to any right as to any property, may institute a suit against any person denying, or interested to deny, his title to such character or right, and the court may in its discretion make therein a declaration that he is so entitled, and the plaintiff need not in such suit ask for any further relief. 

 "A suit for declaration is maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as to any legal character or to any right as to any property of the plaintiff if the defendant denies or is interested to deny his title to such character or right. If the above conditions are satisfied, the plaintiff need not ask for any further relief than a mere declaration." 

 17. In the result the Rule having no merit is discharged without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree dated 27-3-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 250 of 2005 reversing those of dated 19-4-2005 and 26-4-2005 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 352 of 2004 is hereby affirmed.

parties:
Mrs. Begum Aftabuddin Ahmed ------ Defendant-Petitioner.
Vs
Mahmud Alam alias Mahmudul Alam and others ------ Plaintiff-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule have been issued calling upon the Principle-Opposite Party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 12.09.1992 and 19.09.1992 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st  Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 115 of 1987 affirming the judgment and decree dated 26.02.1987 and 05.03.1987 respectively passed by the learned Munsif, Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 73 of 1986 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell, can be stated thus, the plaintiff-opposite party filed the original suit being title suit no. 368 of 1984 in the 1st Court of the then Munsif, Dhaka which was transferred to the Additional Court of Munsif and renumbered as Title Suit No. 73 of 1986 for declaration and permanent injunction contending inter alia that the plaintiff is a bonafide business man who purchased the possession of the suit shop from one Md. Selim at a consideration of Tk. 30,000/- (thirty thousand) on 19.12.1979 and since then he is running his business as a shop of cycle and cycle parts. The plaintiff is a member of Mohammadpur Bazar Committee under Dhaka Metropolitan Area and during the continuance of plaintiff's possession a litigation was cropped up between the market committee and the shop-keepers regarding the recognition of the possessors in the shops. Several meetings were held between the market committee and the representative of the shop-keepers in presence of concerned minister in charge and it was decided that a survey team after physical survey would prepare a list of businessman who are found in occupation of the shops. Accordingly, a survey team was constituted and after survey they .submitted a report to the concern ministry of the Government on 16.03.1981 and the plaintiff's name was listed in serial no. 19. Before final publication of the said list a subsequent survey was held on a dispute by a legally constituted survey team and in the said survey report which was published finally in the year 1984 the name of the plaintiff has been enlisted in serial no. 24. On the basis of that final list the defendant no. 1 who is the Administrative officer, Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Mohammadpur, Dhaka issued an offer letter in favour of the plaintiff on 07.06.1984 asking the plaintiff to deposit Tk. 30,000/-(thirty thousand) as compensation and arrear rent of the suit shop in 3(three) instalments in order to get allotment of the shop. Accordingly the plaintiff paid Tk. 15,000/-(fifteen thousand) of first installment within the prescribed time on 10.06.1984. But on the same date the plaintiff received a letter showing that his allotment offer was issued on mistake and therefore it was cancelled. Being aggrieved by that letter the plaintiff filed the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the contesting defendant is such that the suit-shop is a Government shop at Mohammadpur area which is controlled and managed by the defendants. The defendant no.1 out of mistake issued an offer letter under memo no. 291/A.O. dated 07.06.1984 and after investigation it was found that the letter was issued out of mistake which was cancelled accordingly. The plaintiff was merely asked to deposit Tk. 30,000/- (thirty thousand) as compensation money and the issuance of offer letter does not confer any right, title and interest of the suit-shop in favour of the plaintiff. The Government considering the actual facts issued offer letter to one Mrs. Aftab Uddin Ahmed who is the defendant-respondent-petitioner of this revisional application vide memo no. 316/A.O. dated 10.06.1984. The further case of the contesting defendant is such that the plaintiff is a trespasser in the suit-shop and he has no legal right for getting the allotment letter of the suit shop and the letter of cancellation of the offer of allotment is quite lawful and the plaintiff is not entitled to get relief as prayed for. The learned the then Munsif, Additional Court, Dhaka vide his judgment and decree dated 26.02.1987 decreed the suit in part and declared the letter of cancellation dated 10.06.1984 illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. Being aggrieved the defendant preferred a Title Appeal in the court of learned District Judge, Dhaka being Title Appeal No. 115 of 1987 which was heard and disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge, Is' Court, Dhaka. The learned appellate court after hearing the appeal disallowed the same affirming the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 05.03.1987. 

 6. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and subsequent appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity in deciding the fate of the suit and appeal respectively in favour of the plaintiff. The learned advocate further submits that the part decree of the trial court and the judgment of affirmation by the appellate court below are illegal, invalid and ultravires. The learned court below failed to determine that the plaintiff have got no prima-facie case and right, title, interest in the suit-shop and the issuance of allotment offer by the authority in favour of the plaintiff was a mistake and as soon as the matter was brought into the notice of the concerned authority they cancelled the offer letter which was earlier inadvertently issued in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party. The learned advocate further submits that no title and interest was 'conferred in favour of the plaintiff by issuance of the allotment offer letter and accordingly no contract was effected between the parties. The learned appellate court below misinterpreted the law and failed to assess the evidence on record properly and accordingly committed an error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned advocate for the petitioner lastly submits that the witness no. 1 for the plaintiff Md. Monjur Alam was not legally empowered to depose in favour of the plaintiffs case and his deposition bears no value in the eye of law which is barred under Order III Rule 1 and 2 of the, Code of Civil Procedure. The learned lower appellate court as well as the trial court without considering the very aspect committed illegality and as such the impugned judgment and decree deserve interference of this court. 

 7. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and it's subsequent appeal committed no illegality or irregularity and there is no non-consideration of the material facts and non-reading or misreading of evidence resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned advocate also submits that the defendant in support of his respective case has totally failed to produce any scrap of authentic paper to substantiate his claim in the Suit-shop. The learned advocate further submits that the plaintiff is a bonafide purchaser of possession of suit-shop and in the year 1979 A.D. the plaintiff purchased the possession of the shop from the original owner Mohammad Salim and he is continuing his business therein as a shop of cycle and cycle parts since then. In the year 1981 and 1984 there were two field survey physically by a legally constituted survey team and in both the two survey it was found that the plaintiff do possess the suit-shop and use to run his business therein. The survey teams rightly submitted their report and in first Report in serial no. 19 and in the subsequent Report in serial no. 24 the name of the plaintiff has been enlisted. The Government finding the legal aspect and physical possession of the suit-shop issue an offer of allotment letter and asked the plaintiff to deposit the consideration money. Accordingly., the, plaintiff deposited his first installment within time but subsequently in an arbitrarily and malafide way the defendant no. 1 being influenced by third party issued a cancellation letter stating 'mistake' without any specification and the plaintiff thereafter to redress his grievances filed the original suit which is thoroughly considered by both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and appeal. The learned advocate lastly submits that the appellate court being the final court of fact committed no wrong and rightly assessed the evidence on record properly. The witness no. 1 for the plaintiff Md. Monjur Alam being the father of the plaintiff was quite competent and legally empowered to depose on behalf of his son and under the purview of Order III Rule 2(b) this witness legally deposed in support of the respective case of the plaintiff and hence; there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court. 

 9. On perusal of the case record it transpires that the suit-shop is situated within Mohammadpur area and admittedly the plaintiff-opposite party possess the suit-shop since 1979. It is the case of the defendant that the possession of the plaintiff is unauthorized and he is a trespasser in the suit-shop. I have come across from the evidence on records that the plaintiff Mahmud Alam alias Mahmudul Alam purchased the possession of the suit-shop from one Mohammad Selim in the year 1979. The documentary evidence dated 19.12.1979 has been marked as 'exhibit-1'. The survey report of Mohammadpur Government market and list of market committee which has been marked as 'exhibit-2' supported the case of the plaintiff as to the enlistment of his name as possessor of the suit-shop. Both the courts below in their findings and decisions opined that the possession of the plaintiff in the suit-shop has been reflected by the documents produced and from two legally empowered survey committees for twice the contention of the plaintiff established. Accordingly, the Administrative officer of Mohammadpur Housing Estate issued an offer letter of allotment of the suit-shop in favour of the plaintiff vide memo no. 291/A.O. dated 07.06.1984. Pursuant to the said letter the plaintiff deposited his first installment of Tk. 15,000/- (fifteen thousand) on 10.06.1984 in favour of Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka. On the same date i.e. on 10.06.1984 the disputed cancellation letter was issued by the said authority stating that out of mistake the earlier offer letter of allotment was issued in respect of the suit-shop which was signed by the officer concerned on 07.06.1984 but curiously the memo was issued on 10.06.1984. 1 have come across from the documentary evidence which has been marked as 'exhibit-6' that a title suit being no. 532 of 1974 in which the order of statusquo was passed was dismissed on 01.01.1976. Subsequent to that a miscellaneous case being no. 129 of 1975 was filed for restoration of the suit which was also dismissed for default on 30.04.1984. 

 under Order IX Rule 9 of the Code of Civil .Procedure on 10.05.1984 but there is nothing to show that the case was allowed or the original suit was restored to it's file and number. Therefore, it is evident to note that the order of status quo was no more in existence while the offer letter was issued in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party. On careful scrutiny over the evidence on record it further appears that the witness no. I for the plaintiff corroborated the plaint case and it has come to the notice of the court that at the relevant time the son of this witness the plaintiff was residing at Chittagong and the witness no. 1 Monjur Alam looked after the suit shop and used to run the business therein. He is well acquainted with the suit-shop from the very beginning. The witness no. 2 for the plaintiff is Mirza Mahmud Hasan who is the president of the market committee and in the year 1975 A.D. executive member of the said market committee states at a stage that one Aftab Uddin possessed the suit shop from 1973 to 1975 and thereafter leaving the suit-shop he left the place. This witness also states that the market committee and housing settlement concern to ascertain and recognize the genuine business man who possess the shops surveyed the shops of the market after forming a survey committee and during both the two survey period it was found that the plaintiff is in possession in the suit-shop. This witness also states in his deposition that the plaintiff 'deposited the amount first. The only witness for the defendants is the witness no. 1 Md. Nur Jamal who is an upper division Assistant of housing settlement under Ministry of Housing and Settlement. This witness states specifically at a stage of his testimony that they issued the offer letter in favour of the plaintiff on 07.06.1984 and that letter was cancelled on 10.07.1984. This witness admits that vide exhibit- B and B/1 the plaintiff deposited Tk. 15,000/- (fifteen thousand) as compensation in compliance of their offer letter for allotment. In the cross-examination the sole witness of the defendants in the very beginning states in the following way: একজিবিট-২ এবং ২(এ) সার্ভে রিপোর্ট আমাদের ডিপার্টমেন্ট কর্তৃক করা হয়েছে এবং সার্ভে রিপোর্ট অনুযায়ী অফার লেটার দেই। উক্ত সার্ভে রিপোর্ট এ যারা দখলে আছে তাদের নাম এবং তারা কবে থেকে দখলে আছে তা উল্লেখ আছে।" In another stage of his deposition this witness states, ‘‘দুটি সার্ভে রিপোর্ট এ বাদী দখলে আছে বিধায় অফার লেটার দিয়েছিলাম। সার্ভে রিপোর্ট অনুযায়ী দখলকারীদেরকে অফার লেটার দেয়া হয়েছি। বে-দখলকারীদের অফার লেটার দেয়া হয় নাই।" 

 16. The impugned judgment and decree dated 12.09.1992 and 19.09.1992 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 115 of 1987 affirming those of dated 26.02.1987 and 05.03.1987 respectively passed by the learned Munsif, Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 73 of 1986 is hereby affirmed.

2. The facts involved in the case, in short, are that the properties in C.S. Khatian No. 26, C.S. Plot No. 164, S.A. Khatian No. 153, S.A. Plot No. 270 was originally belonged to Ali Baksha and his name has been recorded in C.S. Khatian for an area of 1.58 acres of land; that said Baksha alias Ali Miah died leaving son Abed Ali and three daughters namely Hazera Khatoon, Hasimonnessa and Solemannessa and their names were recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 153, S.A Plot No. 270 for an area of 1.48 acres of land; that Solemannessa transferred his share in favour of Hasimonnessa and Hazera Khatoon on 02.07.1958 vide deed No. 8262 for an are of 16.5 decimals of land, Mostafa on 29.11.1965 vide deed No. 11820 for an area of 11 decimals of land, Md. Sirajul Islam on 29.11.1965 vide deed No. 11819 for an area of 16.5 decimals of land. Thereafter, on 23.06.1993 Sirajul Islam transfer in favour of Md. Mohiuddin Mollah and Khairuzzaman vide deed No. 1786 an area of 6.60 ajutangsha of land Malek Hossain on 23.06.1993 vide deed No. 1785 for an area of 669 ajuntangsh of land, Sheikh Moshiur Rahman on 23.06.1993 being deed No. 1787 for an area of 3.55 ajutangsha of land; that Hasimonnessa transferred his share in favour of Mostafa on 21.10.1965 and Saheda Begum on 20.10.1965 being deed No. 7347 and Mostafa transferred his share in Hafez on 02.06.1976 and thereafter Hafez again transferred in favour of Azizur Rahman on 31.05.1976 vide deed No. 10559 and on 15.06.1976 vide deed No. 11648. Thereafter, Azizur Rahman transferred through his attorney on 22.10.2006 vide deed No. 9872 in favour of Maksuda Begum for 303 ajutangsha of land. Abed Ali Hajee transferred to Solemannessa on 11.01.1979 vide deed No. 407 for an area of 8 decimals of land who transferred to Delwar Hossain on 10.08.1979 and Anisur Rahman Patwary on 10.08.1979 vide deed Nos. 11597 and 11596 for an area of 4 decimals of land each. Hezera Khatoon transferred her share on 27.02.1979 in favour of A.K.M. Rezwan Ali, Safayet Ali and Asgar Ali by three separate deeds being Nos. 1874, 1872 and 1873 respectively. 

 6. It appears the writ-petitioners purchased the land in 1986, which they claim was not acquired by the writ-respondents by L.A. Case No. 66 of 1957-58. It appears from their produced photocopies of title deeds which do not trace their title back to the original owner. Moreover, the disputed questions of title and facts are involved in this case which cannot be dealt with under the summary Jurisdiction.
