parties:
Serajul Huq and others ------- Appellants
Vs. 
Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Work and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment: 2. Brief facts for disposal of this appeal are that the appellants and their predecessors filed the above Case No. 566 of 1987 in the Court of Settlement Dhaka stating that their predecessor Md Hanif migrated from India to the then East Pakistan along with his wife Alima Khatoon and son Serajul Huq, the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 in the above case, and his other two sons ShamsuI Huq and Aynul Huq, the petitioner Nos. 3 and 4 in the above case who are the appellant Nos. 2 and 3 herein, were born in Bangladesh; Md Hanif, who was a Government servant, having retired from service in the year 1964, had been living in Bangladesh with his family as citizens thereof and while drawing pension from the Exchequer of the Government as a retired Government servant he died at Mirpur, Dhaka on 3-9-1981 leaving behind the petitioners in the above case as his successors and to that effect the above successors, Alima Khatoon, Serajul Huq, Shamsul Huq and Aynul Huq, also obtained a certificate from the Court of District Delegate Judge, Dhaka in Succession Certificate Case No. 365 of 1985; Md Hanif who drew pension money from the exchequer of the Government up to 31-8-81, was the owner in possession of a house situated at Plot No. 43, Road No.2, Block B, Section-I, Mirpur Housing Estate, Mirpur, Dhaka, which he got under a lease deed dated 1-12-1961 for a period of 99 years on payment of full cost of Taka 2700 to the Government; while the said Md Hanif and his wife and sons were in peaceful possession of the said house, Bangladesh was liberated on December 16, 1971 followed by some law and order situation and in the abnormal circumstances, then prevailing, Md Hanif and his wife and sons were dispossessed from the said house in the last week of March, 1972 by the anti-social elements who also looted their belongings and household effects including the original documents of title and occupied the above house; during his life time Md Hanif made several representations to different authorities for release of the said house from the list of abandoned properties but in vain and he died on 3-9-1981; thereafter the said house being enlisted in "Ka" list as an abandoned property the above Alima Khatoon, Serajul Huq, Shamsul Huq and Aynul Huq filed application under section 7 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance 1985, Ordinance No. 54 of 1985, for release of the said house from Ka List which was registered as Settlement Case No. 566 of 1987 in the Court of Settlement, Dhaka and the respondents herein, who were the opposite parties in the above case, did not contest the above case and after hearing the Court of Settlement dismissed the case. As against that the above heirs of Md Hanif moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Writ Petition No. 321 of 1989 and the High Court Division, after hearing, discharged the Rule holding, inter alia, that the above heirs failed to rebut the presumption regarding the abandoned character of the above house. In the meantime Alima Khatoon died.

parties:
Abdul Karim and others ------ Petitioner
vs
Court of Settlement and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case as stated in the petition are that the House No. 1/15, Block-D, Razia Sultana Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka, measuring an area of 144 square yards originally belonged to the then Government of East Pakistan and that the Government leased out the aforesaid property to Syed Md Yunus by a registered deed of lease being No. 2067 dated 2-2-1960; that after taking delivery of possession of the aforesaid property the original allottee Syed Md Yunus built a two-storied building on the leasehold land and had been living therein with his family members and that said Syed Md Yunus being in need of urgent cash money sold out the aforesaid building to Md Abdul Quayum by a registered deed being No. 881 dated 3-2-1969 and delivered physical possession of the building in question to said Abdul Quayum and that thereafter, Abdul Quayum while was in ownership and possession of the property he again sold out the same to one Habiba Banu wife of Abdul Ash by a registered deed being No. 3998 dated 30-4-1970 and handed over the physical possession of the house to her on the same day on 30-4-1970; that Habiba Banu, while was in ownership and possession of the aforesaid house she being in need of money sold out the same to the petitioners at a consideration of Taka 40,000 (Taka forty thousand) vide four registered sale deeds being Nos. 2498, 2499, 2500 and 2501 dated 9-12-1972 and handed over the physical possession of the case property along with all original documents of the building in question; that thereafter, aforesaid Habiba Banu left the property and shifted her family to a rented house situated at 22 Bangshal Road, under PS Kotwali, District-Dhaka. The petitioners also stated that Abdul Ash, the husband of Habiba Banu, was a Bangladesh national and a resident of village Ashugonj, under PS and District Brahmanbaria, that the petitioners mutated their names in the office of the City Corporation and got electricity, gas and WASA connection in the case property in their own names and Khatians in respect of the case property has been opened in their names and they have been paying taxes and other bills regularly; that while the petitioners were in ownership and possession of the case property the State Officer under the Ministry of Public Works entered into a lease agreement on 10-4-1974 with Abdul Halim, father of the petitioner, in respect of the case property for the residential accommodation of a Government officer and that after hiring the property the government allotted the same to one Mr Md Arifur Rahman, Administrative Officer, Ministry of Planning, Government of Bangladesh on 30-5-1974 for a period of leone) year and that the said agreement was renewed from time to time upto 1987 and paid rent regularly to the petitioners; that after the death of their father, aforesaid Abdul Halirn, petitioner's mother Rahima Khatun accepted the rent from the Government on behalf of the petitioners. The petitioners filed an application to the Assistant Commissioner of Housing and Settlement, Ministry of Public Works, Segunbagicha, Dhaka on 23-1-1984 and 12-4-1984 for mutating their names in place of the previous owner. On receipt of the applications the Assistant Commissioners held an inquiry through their local Administrative Officer who after holding inquiry submitted a report on 25-4-1985 stating that the petitioners are in possession of the case property by purchase from Habiba Banu. The petitioners further stated that they are in exclusive ownership and possession of the case property by purchase from lawful owner but the Government has published a Gazette on 23-9-1986 enlisting the abandoned building and in the said list the house of the petitioners has been included in the kha list of the abandoned building. The petitioners thereafter filed an application before the Court of Settlement under section 7 of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 for the exclusion of the property from the Kha list which was registered as Settlement case No. 172 of 1995. The Court of Settlement after hearing by judgment and order dated 28-5-2000 rejected the case and thereby refused to exclude the case property from the abandoned list. Being aggrieved thereby the petitioners moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 4. Mr MA Quddus Sheikh, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submitted that the Court of Settlement has taken adverse inference about the title deeds of the petitioners without taking into consideration that those are registered deeds and have got some presumptive value and, as such, the judgment passed by the Court of Settlement is not lawful and the same has got no legal effect. Mr Quddus thereafter, submitted that the Court of Settlement did not consider that the respondent being satisfied with the title of the petitioners hired the same from the petitioners for their residential accommodation and they paid rent to the petitioners and, as such, the judgment and order passed by the Court of Settlement refusing to release the case property from abandoned list is liable to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority. Mr Quddus Sheikh lastly submitted that the property has been included in the 'Kha' list of the abandoned buildings without serving any notice for taking or surrendering possession of the same to the respondents. 

 6. Admittedly, the case property was leased out to one Syed Yunus on 2-2-1960 by the then Government of East Pakistan. It is also admitted that said Md Yunus subsequently sold the case property to Md Abdul, Quayum through registered deed dated 3-2-1969 and while he was in possession in the case property he again sold the same to one Habiba Banu, wife of Md Ash through registered. deed dated 30-4-1970. The case of the petitioners is, that said Habiba Banu sold the case property to these petitioners vide four registered sale deeds dated 9-12-1972 and handed over physical possession to them and that said Habiba Banu also, handed over all original documents in respect of the case property to the petitioners and thereafter, she shifted her family members to 22 Bangshal Road under PS Kotwali, Dhaka, and that Habiba Banu never left this country during the liberation war and her whereabouts was not unknown. The petitioners have submitted all the original documents including the original lease deed and lease agreement granted by the then Government of East Pakistan in favour of the original allottee Syed Md Yunus. The original deed of subsequent purchasers Md Abdul Quayum and thereafter Abdul Quayum to Habiba Banu have also been annexed as Annexure-D and D1 respectively with this writ petition. Four title deeds of the petitioners have also been annexed as Annexure-E Series. The petitioners thereafter mutated their names in the office of the Dhaka City Corporation and took gas, electricity and WASA connection in their own names and copy of the same has been annexed as Annexure-F series. 

 7. The Court of Settlement rejected the case of petitioners holding, that the LTI of Habiba Banu, the vendor of the petitioners, appearing in the title deed of the petitioners, is not product of the same hand and that some of the LTI are highly indistinct, some contain most insufficient ink and that none of the attesting witnesses of the title deeds of the petitioners have been examined to prove the genuineness of those deeds. The respondents did not submit any written objection before the Court of Settlement and they have also failed to produce the concerned file regarding the abandoned house. The Court of Settlement lastly held that the petitioners have failed to prove that Habiba Banu ever sold the case property to them through their title deeds. Specific case of the petitioners is that they purchased the case property from Habiba Banu and while they were in ownership and possession of the case property they let out the said house to the Government for the residential accommodation of an Administrative Officer of the Ministry of Planning, Government of Bangladesh vide Arlnexure-G(1) an agreement dated 10-4-1974 and thereafter, the said house was allotted to Md M Arifur Rahman on 30- 5-1974. From the said annexures it appears that one Abdul Halim signed the said agreement on behalf of the landlord. These petitioners claim that this Abdul Halim is their father. In their title deeds the petitioners have mentioned their father's name as Abdul Halim. After the death of aforesaid Abdul Halim the mother of the petitioners Rahima Khatun received rents of the house in question from the Government on behalf of the petitioners. The respondents have not denied that the property was sold to Md Abdul Quayum by the original lessee Syed Md Yunus and that Abdul Quayum thereafter sold the case property to Habiba Banu. 

 8. The respondents only stated that Habiba Banu never sold the case property to the petitioners in the year 1972 remaining herself in possession of the case property. The respondent No. 2 hired the case property for residential accommodation of their officers vide Annexure-G1 and paid rent to the petitioners. We get support of the said fact from the documents filed by the respondent No. 2 as Annexure-1 series along with the supplementary affidavit dated 1-2-2007. Annexure-1 is a letter dated 7-12-2006 sent by the Assistant Director of the Government Accommodation Directorate, to the learned Deputy Attorney-General stating that the case property was hired by their Directorate at a rent of Taka 1350 from 1-7-1983 and was allotted and that the case file of the property is not traceable from their office. Annexure-1A is a rent receipt which shows that the rent of the house in question was paid to (Halima Khatun) mother of the petitioners) on 1-7-1983. Annexure-I(b) is an attested photo copy of the rent receiving register which shows that the respondent paid rent against the case property for several months to Rahima Khatun. On being directed by the Court the learned Deputy Attorney-General has produced the rent receipt register of the Accommodation Directorate in original. From pages 4376 and 4377 it appears that Rahima Khatunis the owner of the house situated at 1/15 Razia Sultana Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka which is the case property and the Government paid rent to Rahima Khatun for several months in the year 1983 and 84. The learned Advocate for the petitioners orally submitted that the Government after 1984 did not extend rent agreement and handed over the vacant possession to the petitioners and since then they are in possession of the case property. The respondents though claimed that the Government took possession of the case property in the year 1972 but they are quite silent as to how the petitioners thereafter went into possession of the case property. The petitioners have submitted all the original documents including their title deeds. The Court of Settlement without going through the contents of those documents held, that the LTI alleged to have been put by Habiba Banu in the title deeds of the petitioners do not tally with each other and the same are not the product of same hand. We have examined the title deeds of the petitioners Annexure-E series. From the LTI of those deeds it cannot be said that those are not the products of same hand. We did not find any reason to disbelieve the execution and registration of those title deeds by Habiba Banu in favour of the petitioners. The Court of Settlement was not justified in discarding those title deeds without obtaining any expert opinion from a fingerprint expert to ascertain the genuineness of LTI of Habiba Banu. In the case of Tarak Chandra Majhi vs Atahar Ali Howlader and others reported in 8 BLC (AD) 67 their Lordships held that- 

 The petitioners had filed all the original documents before the Court of Settlement and the court did not make any doubt about the genuineness of the original documents but rejected the case only on the ground that the LTI of Habiba Banu put in the title deeds of the petitioners do not tally with each other. This finding of the Court of Settlement is not lawful. Since the original documents have been produced by the petitioners, it was the duty of the Court of Settlement to come to a finding about the genuineness of those documents after obtaining the expert opinion on the LTI of Habib a Banu with her admitted signature. The Court of settlement dis- believed the title deeds of the petitioners on the ground that some of the LTI are highly indistinct and some contain excess ink. For this indistinct and excess ink in the LTI of vendor of the petitioners in the title deeds it cannot be said that those were not executed by the vendor or the same cannot be disbelieved.

parties:
Sayeda Shajada Hossain & another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Wega Fashion Sweater (Pvt) Ltd & ors ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
3. The respondent No.8 (appellant in CA No. 62 of 2004) by filing affidavit-in-opposition contested the Rule and controverted the material allegations made in the writ petition and further contended, inter alia, that the writ petition involved complicated questions of fact as to title and also as to possession and dispossession which could not be decided without filing a proper suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession and, as such, the writ petition is not maintainable. The MLO No.128 of 86 dated 13-5-1986 having been issued by the then Chief Martial Law Authority, the same was protected under Act No, 1 of 1986 and, as such, writ petition does not lie against the said MLO No. 128/86 and no relief touching the decision of any matter relating to the said MLO can be given in the writ petition. The further case is that the writ petitioners are joint owners of 17 decimals of land out of 1.25 acres of land of CS Plot No. 177 or otherwise in possession of the same upon mutation of their names and upon payment of rent and taxes and that they were illegally dispossessed on 16-10-2000 are all denied by the appellant. The further case is that the writ petitioners were not in possession and, as such, the question of dispossession by the appellant did not arise, and they are also not owners of the land of CS Plot No. 177. The entire land of CS Plot No. 177 under CS Khatian No. 49 of Mouza Begunbari, PS Tejgaon, Dhaka and other lands of the same Mouza were requisitioned by Government by order dated 28-9-1959 and 25-2-1960 under section 3 of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 and the said property continued to be subject of requisition. Later on, the said land was acquired by the Government in LA Case No. 1611959-1960 and rightly vested in the Government free from all encumbrances and the right, title and interest if any, of the original owners extinguished. The allegation that the lands were subsequently derequisitioned are false and concocted. Therefore, the question of treating the same as vested property (enemy property) or releasing the same by the Ministry of Land does not arise. There is no law authorising the Government to release any land once it vested in the Government by acquisition according to law. 

 4. The respondent No.1, Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land and respondent No.5, Sub-Divisional Engineer, Public Works Department, Dhaka by filing joint affidavit-in-opposition contested the Rule denying the material allegations made in the writ petition and further contended that complicated questions of title and possession and dispossession being involved the writ petition is not maintainable. The CS Plot No. 177 of Mouza Begunbari, PS Tejgaon, Dhaka is acquired land of the Government under the supervision and management of the respondent No.5 and the allegation of dispossession of the writ petitioners on 16-10-2000 is false. The vacant possession of the land in question had been delivered to the respondent No.8 of the writ petition (appellant in CA No. 62 of 2004) by the respondent No.5 of the writ petition on 12-10-2000. 

 7. From the judgment sought to be reviewed it is clear that this question was duly considered and it was held that since the case land along with other lands of CS Plot No. 177 of Mouza Begunbari, PS Tejgaon, Dhaka was acquired by the Government in LA Case No. 16 of 1959-60, the same absolutely vested in the Government free from all encumbrances and the right, title and interest, if any, of the original owners extinguished. It was also held that the Government had no authority to release the property under the law in favour of either the original owner or anybody else and Government may also use such land for similar other public purposes.
